title: The Mordell conjecture after Lawrence and Venkatesh, Part II
summary: This roadmap unifies two higher-dimensional continuations of the Lawrence–Venkatesh method. Compatible cohomological realizations and semilinear coefficient groups turn global representation finiteness into local period conditions. Balanced filtrations and adjoint Hodge estimates make those conditions sufficiently small. The applications are non-density for high-dimensional projective hypersurface parameters and Shafarevich finiteness, up to rational translation, for smooth ample hypersurfaces in abelian varieties.
readme: The definitive reader is research/blueprint/readmes/MordellLawrenceVenkateshPartII.md. It gives the shared tensor, monodromy and codimension mechanism, the distinct geometric applications, exact supplier contracts, and discriminating checks. The first-generation Mordell roadmap supplies arithmetic GL finiteness and global pure-character weights. SheafConvolutionOnAbelianVarieties supplies convolution monodromy, torsion-orbit selection and exceptional degrees. The planning pass is complete; the dependency graph has recorded gaps and is not closed.

stages.title: Compatible Hodge–Deligne realizations
stages.description:
Assemble the four compatible realizations, their tensor category, geometric projector systems, differential monodromy and fixed Frobenius data on residue disks.

Hodge–Deligne systems. Fix a number field K, an embedding K→C, a smooth geometrically connected K-variety X with smooth model 𝓧/O_K[S⁻¹], and a rational prime p below no place of S, unramified in K, with v|p. A Hodge–Deligne system consists of a finite-rank Q local system on X(C), a continuous Q_p local system on 𝓧[1/p], a filtered finite locally free bundle with integrable connection on X, and a filtered F-isocrystal on the v-adic tube, with Betti–étale, Betti–de Rham, crystalline–de Rham and structural O B_cris comparisons. These preserve tensor operations, connection, filtrations and a finite weight filtration W. Require regular singularities, Griffiths transversality and fibrewise pure Hodge and Weil-weight conditions on gr_W. Rational Weil numbers need not be integral; polarization and a Z-lattice are additional conditions.

Integral and polarized systems. For a Hodge–Deligne system, integral means a locally constant finite free Z lattice in its Betti realization spanning it over Q. Polarized means pure of a specified weight and equipped with a flat rational bilinear polarization of its variation of Hodge structure. Integral Frobenius means that, at every relevant closed point away from S and p and in the crystalline realization, Frobenius eigenvalues are algebraic integers. These are three separate predicates; integral Frobenius is not preserved by arbitrary duals.

Tensor category of compatible systems. Over the fixed connected base of M2.0, morphisms are maps of all four realizations compatible with W, F, connection, Frobenius and all comparisons. With componentwise tensor products, duals, direct sums and the unit, Hodge–Deligne systems form a Q-linear neutral Tannakian category under evaluation of the Betti realization at a chosen complex point. Prove strictness of the filtrations and that the componentwise kernels and cokernels again satisfy the axioms; do not treat arbitrary filtered vector spaces as an abelian category.

Constant arithmetic systems. A constant Hodge–Deligne system on 𝓧 is a pullback of a system over Spec O_K[S⁻¹]. The trivial coefficient system O_E for a finite-dimensional Q-algebra E has constant Betti E, trivial arithmetic Galois action on E⊗Q_p, trivial connection and degree-zero Hodge filtration, and Frobenius 1_E⊗σ_v. A constant arithmetic system may have nontrivial arithmetic Galois action; constancy here means trivial geometric variation.

Geometric cohomology and projectors. For a smooth projective morphism f:Y→X extending smoothly and projectively over the model, construct the compatible system R^k f_*Q using Betti, étale, algebraic de Rham and crystalline cohomology. A compatible finite-group idempotent in the rational endomorphisms cuts out a direct-summand system; intersect its rational Betti image with an integral cohomology lattice modulo torsion to obtain a spanning lattice. Pure cohomological systems are polarized and have integral Frobenius eigenvalues. The general coefficient pushforward in LS Example 5.10 additionally requires a relative coefficient-comparison theorem, recorded as a gap rather than inferred from constant coefficients.

Differential monodromy from a tensor generator. Let V be a system on a smooth geometrically connected X/K with chosen K-rational fibre point, or after a stated finite extension supplying one. Define G_mon as the tensor automorphism group of the fibre functor on the rigid abelian tensor category generated by (V_dR,∇). Regular-singular Riemann–Hilbert identifies its base change to C with the Zariski closure of Betti geometric monodromy on V. Transport between fibre choices is by the tensor-isomorphism torsor, so the resulting groups are defined up to inner identification; no unrelated Picard–Vessiot theory is developed.

Constant Frobenius data on a residue disk. On a smooth v-adic residue disk Ω of a system, parallel transport of its convergent F-isocrystal identifies all underlying crystalline pairs with one finite-dimensional (V,φ), with φ semilinear for the residue Frobenius. Its Hodge filtrations F_x vary analytically, giving Φ_p:Ω→Flag(V). This is a local statement on the tube with compatible Frobenius transport, not a globally constant crystal.

stages.title: Arithmetic coefficient systems
stages.description:
Build H⁰-algebras, module and classical structures, torsion-character orbit cohomology and its polarization. Prove rational Frobenius characteristic polynomials for the geometric orbit system as a separate arithmetic input.

Étale H⁰-algebras. An H⁰-algebra is a commutative unital algebra object E in the system category, pure of weight zero with F⁰E_dR=E_dR and F¹E_dR=0. It is étale when its Betti Q-algebra is finite étale. In the arithmetic argument require E to be constant in the arithmetic-pullback sense. Its étale realization can have a nontrivial finite Galois permutation action.

Finite étale coefficient operations. Construct H⁰-algebras from the trivial algebra O_E, the rational group algebra Q[B] of a finite abelian group B, the function algebra on a finite étale commutative group scheme, R⁰ of a proper smooth family, and pushforward along a finite étale base map. In the finite-monodromy case define crystalline realization by D_cris of the actual Galois representation. If K_v/Q_p is unramified of degree f, its semilinear Frobenius satisfies φ^f equal, under the unramified comparison, to the representation action of geometric Frobenius; the naive formula using the same residue-Frobenius action on both factors is not imposed.

Modules over coefficient algebras. An E-module system is a system V with a unital action E⊗V→V compatible with the four realizations. Define E-linear maps and the relative tensor product as the cokernel of the two E-actions on V⊗E⊗W; for finite étale E this is exact in either module argument. A bilinear pairing valued in an invertible rank-one E-module L is E-balanced when B(ev,w)=B(v,ew).

Equidimensional coefficient modules. For a finite étale E over a field E₀, V is equidimensional of rank N when V⊗_(E,τ)Ē₀ has dimension N for every embedding τ:E→Ē₀. For a system require the same condition on its realizations; equivalently each is a free E-realization module of rank N. This is not constancy of the total E₀-dimension alone.

General linear, symplectic and orthogonal structures. For an equidimensional E-module V of positive rank N, a GL_N structure is its E-linear structure alone. A GSp_N structure is a perfect alternating E-bilinear pairing V⊗_E V→L with L invertible of E-rank one, requiring N even. A GO_N structure uses a perfect symmetric pairing into such an L. Isomorphisms include the compatible similitude on L. Keep the whole orthogonal similitude group, which need not be connected.

Finite-order character systems. Let A be an abelian scheme over O_K[S⁻¹], r invertible there, and χ a finite-order character of A[r] after a finite étale splitting extension, with values in Q(μ_r). Pulling back the character summand of [r]_*Q gives a rank-one Q(μ_r)-module system L_χ. Descent includes both Galois transport of the torsion character and cyclotomic transport of its values; a primitive character need not define a rank-one Q system.

Galois-orbit cohomology systems. Let Y⊂X_K×A be a smooth projective family of hypersurfaces, X smooth over Q with suitable integral model and O_K[S⁻¹] finite étale over Z[S′⁻¹]. Let I be a finite orbit of pairs (ι,χ) under Gal(Q̄/Q)×Gal(Q^cyc/Q), with χ of order r prime to p, for which twisted cohomology vanishes outside degree n−1. Construct a constant finite étale H⁰-algebra E_I on X with geometric idempotents indexed by I, and an E_I-module system V_I whose geometric coefficient fibres are R^(n−1)f_(ι)*g_(ι)^*L_χ. Its E_I-rank is N=n!d when d=[H]^n/n!, and its Q-rank is |I|N. It is integral, pure polarized of weight n−1, and integral-Frobenius.

Inversion and the coefficient-linear pairing. For an orbit system whose generic hypersurface is invariant under inversion up to translation, construct the resulting involution i and the pairing (v,w)↦⟨v,iw⟩. It is E-balanced, perfect, and valued in an invertible E-module. For ambient dimension n even it is alternating and gives GSp_N; for n odd it is symmetric and gives GO_N. All translation and coefficient descent data must be carried along; the original pairing that couples χ and χ⁻¹ is not itself asserted E-bilinear.

Rational Frobenius polynomials for geometric orbit systems. For the full arithmetic/cyclotomic orbit system V_I constructed as a rational finite-group projector of multiplication-cover cohomology, its geometric Frobenius characteristic polynomials at good primes of the arithmetic Galois realization have rational coefficients and algebraic-integer roots, hence lie in Z[t]. Prove rationality using traces of powers of Frobenius composed with the rational group-correspondence projector and the fixed-point trace formula. This additional geometric assertion supplies the stronger arithmetic finiteness interface; it is not part of the definition of an arbitrary Hodge–Deligne system.

stages.title: Semilinear groups and filtered tensor objects
stages.description:
Specialize the existing algebraic-group theory to coefficient normalizers, semisimplification and crystalline inner forms. Define finite adjoint profiles, top-weight sums and uniformity, and establish the global-type and parabolic/Levi finiteness targets.

Semilinear coefficient normalizers. Let E/E₀ be finite étale in characteristic zero, V free of E-rank N>0, and H=GL_N, GSp_N or GO_N in its standard representation (with a perfect E-valued form after a line trivialization in the paired cases). Set B=Res_(E/E₀)H and G=N_(GL_(E₀)(V))(B). Identify G with invertible E-semilinear maps, respecting the form up to a semilinear similitude in the paired cases. Obtain 1→B→G→Aut_(E₀)(E)→1 as a group-scheme exact sequence, surjective fppf-locally. B is not renamed the identity component when H=GO_(2r).

Semilinear Frobenius centralizer bound. In the preceding setup, if σ∈Aut_(E₀)(E) has fixed algebra E^σ=E₀ and φ∈G is σ-semilinear, then dim Z_G(φ)≤dim H. More generally on each σ-cycle of geometric coefficient factors, projection of Z_B(φ) to any one factor is injective, so the bound is one factor dimension per cycle.

Semisimplification in the coefficient normalizer. For the specific normalizer G of M2.2 and a subgroup Γ⊂G over a characteristic-zero field, use Richardson parabolics P_λ={g:lim_(t→0)λ(t)gλ(t)⁻¹ exists}, their Levi quotients and unipotent radicals. Γ is G-completely reducible when every such P_λ containing Γ has a Levi containing Γ. Projecting Γ from a minimal containing P_λ to its Levi gives a G-completely reducible subgroup, unique up to G-conjugacy after the source-qualified field extension. For Γ a representation image call this its G-semisimplification. Rational conjugacy and continuity require separate descent, not merely geometric closed-orbit uniqueness.

Tensor G-structures. For an affine algebraic group G/k and a k-linear tensor category C with a fibre functor ω, a G-object is an exact faithful k-linear symmetric monoidal functor Rep_fd(G)→C together with a tensor trivialization of its composite with ω to the forgetful functor. Changing the trivialization conjugates the resulting homomorphism of Tannaka groups. A faithful representation with defining tensors describes the same structure only after proving the tensor reconstruction comparison.

Tensor filtrations and cocharacters. For G in characteristic zero with reductive identity component, a G-filtration is an exact tensor-compatible filtration of the forgetful functor Rep_fd(G)→Vect, with the canonical associated-graded tensor structure. A splitting cocharacter μ gives F^aV=⊕_(j≥a)V_j. Two cocharacters define the same filtration precisely when their dynamic parabolics agree and they are conjugate in that parabolic. Restriction to G° identifies G-filtrations with G°-filtrations, but a parabolic alone records a filtration only up to indexing. On descending filtrations gr^a=F^a/F^(a+1).

Crystalline tensor structures and inner forms. For a crystalline G-valued local Galois representation over Q_p with G in the preceding class, D_cris applied as an exact tensor functor gives filtered φ-data with an inner form G′ and a G′-filtration. A homomorphism G₁→G₂ induces a homomorphism between the corresponding inner forms, compatible with tensors. In the coefficient-normalizer case identify G′ with the de Rham coefficient normalizer through the actual realization comparison. There is no canonical equality G′=G for an arbitrary G-object.

Adjoint Hodge profiles and top-weight sums. Given a G-filtration on a characteristic-zero group, define h^a=dim gr^a Lie(G), a finitely supported sequence of natural numbers. In the polarized weight-zero adjoint case h^a=h^(−a). Put D=Σ_a h^a, A=Σ_(a>0)h^a, B=Σ_(a>0)a h^a. Order the D weights with multiplicities nonincreasingly as w₁,…,w_D. For real x∈[0,D], define T(x)=Σ_(j≤floor x)w_j+(x−floor x)w_(floor x+1), with T(D)=Σ_j w_j. Thus T is continuous piecewise linear, with each weight appearing h^a times; it does not sum the multiplicities themselves.

Uniform coefficient filtrations. For a filtration of a coefficient-normalizer object, uniform means that the adjoint Hodge profile on H is the same at every geometric embedding of its finite étale coefficient algebra. If [E:E₀]=d, its restriction-of-scalars profile is d times the single-factor profile; in particular T_Res(dx)=dT_H(x). The numerical inequalities of the non-density theorem always use h_H,T_H, not the scaled restriction-of-scalars profile.

Finiteness of global coefficient-group types. Fix p, a finite T containing p, and the coefficient normalizer G/Q_p of M2.2 with its fixed faithful standard representation and coefficient permutation action. Fix rank and an integer pure Weil weight w≥0. Continuous G-completely reducible representations G_Q→G(Q_p), unramified outside T and having characteristic polynomials in Z[t] with weight-w roots at Frobenius outside T, form finitely many G(Q_p)-conjugacy classes. Rational-orbit descent and the possibly disconnected GO coefficient group require the inputs recorded as gaps. This target extends the parent GL finiteness theorem; it is not inferred from finite GL-conjugacy classes alone.

Finitely many semisimplification geometries. Let G be a characteristic-zero algebraic group with reductive identity component and H⊂G a G-completely reducible subgroup. Up to the action of Z_G(H), only finitely many pairs (P,M) occur with P a Richardson parabolic, M a Levi of P and H⊂M. Consequently a fixed completely reducible image gives finitely many parabolic/Levi semisimplification types. This is a finiteness statement up to centralizer conjugacy, not finiteness of actual parabolics.

stages.title: Period orbits and transcendence transfer
stages.description:
Identify a monodromy period orbit with parabolic stabilizer, apply the externally supplied pure integral Ax–Schanuel theorem componentwise, and transfer its codimension consequence to p-adic non-density through analytic radicals and Krull intersection.

Periods in a single monodromy orbit. The complex and p-adic period maps of a compatible system, after the stated fibre identifications, lie in one orbit of its differential monodromy group in the relevant compact dual. The orbit is defined by the horizontal tensor relations of the tensor category generated by the connection. Over a nonclosed field use its tensor-isomorphism torsor; do not choose a rational trivialization without an existence argument.

Parabolic stabilizers of period orbits. For a polarized pure variation, the stabilizer of its Hodge filtration inside the connected algebraic monodromy group is parabolic; its orbit is consequently projective. Use normality of connected monodromy in the derived generic Mumford–Tate group and the Hodge cocharacter action. Pass to a positive power of the cocharacter if needed to lift the induced inner action; finite disconnected components do not change the connected orbit.

Analytic radicals for period ideals. Let Φ be a local holomorphic period map in smooth coordinates at x and I the ideal of convergent germs defining Φ⁻¹(Z). If an algebraic function g on the smooth base vanishes on that germ, some power g^m lies in I. Obtain this exact membership statement from the local analytic Nullstellensatz in ComplexComparisonPartII C0; the general theorem I(V(I))=√I is a requested supplier extension, not a second construction here.

Algebraic degeneracy from period codimension. Let X be smooth irreducible over C of positive dimension d and let its pure polarized integral variation have connected monodromy period orbit D_mon. If an algebraic subset Z⊂D_mon has codimension at least d, every positive-dimensional irreducible analytic component of the inverse image of Z under a local period map is contained in a proper algebraic subvariety of X. Zero-dimensional local components are points and are also proper. The assertion is componentwise or germwise; it does not assert that infinitely many components have one common proper algebraic closure.

Transfer to p-adic non-density. Let X/Q be smooth geometrically connected of positive dimension d, with a pure polarized integral compatible system, and fix a smooth p-adic residue disk Ω and its monodromy period orbit. For an algebraic Z in that orbit of codimension at least d, Φ_p⁻¹(Z)∩Ω is not Zariski dense in X. After shrinking to affinoid subdisks the assertion combines finitely many minimal primes; finitely many residue disks combine by taking a product of nonzero algebraic equations.

stages.title: Balanced monodromy and semisimple fibres
stages.description:
Describe the subdirect-product index partition, strong balance on every Frobenius orbit and the torsion-orbit comparison. Bound fixed semisimple filtration loci and deduce non-density for semisimple integral fibres.

Index classes of subdirect monodromy. Let H be a connected semisimple characteristic-zero group with simple adjoint quotient and let L⊂H^I be a closed subgroup surjective onto each factor, for finite nonempty I. Put i~j when the projection to factors i,j is not the full product, allowing the equivalent graph-of-an-isogeny formulation after central quotients. This is an equivalence relation. Projection onto one representative of each class is surjective with finite kernel. Apply to SL_N (N≥2), Sp_2r (r≥1), and SO_N (N=3 or N≥5); SO₂ and SO₄ require separate treatment and are excluded.

Strongly balanced monodromy. For the preceding index partition and integer c≥1, c-balanced means all classes have equal cardinality and there are at least c classes. Given a permutation σ of I, strongly c-balanced additionally means σ preserves the partition and every σ-orbit meets at least c distinct classes. For a subgroup of the coefficient group, apply this condition to its intersection with the product of derived classical factors after algebraic closure. Neither the scalar centres nor the similitude characters supply the independent directions.

Torsion-orbit monodromy is strongly balanced. For a nonconstant-up-to-translation family of primitive smooth ample hypersurfaces satisfying the supplied classical-monodromy hypotheses, the orbit character supplied by SC.8 can be chosen so that its coefficient cohomology system has strongly c-balanced differential monodromy relative to residue Frobenius, for any prescribed c≥1. Normal containment of c independent derived factors, after the stated Frobenius powers and for every arithmetic/cyclotomic conjugate, supplies the orbitwise condition. Use the algebraically closed extension comparison to return to the de Rham group.

Codimension of semisimple isomorphism orbits. Let a uniform coefficient filtration have single-factor profile h and strongly c-balanced monodromy relative to σ. Suppose E^σ=E₀ on the chosen Frobenius cycle, e>0 and A≥(e+dim H)/c. In the monodromy flag orbit, the locus whose filtered Frobenius module is isomorphic to a prescribed one has codimension at least e. More generally select one σ-cycle meeting c index classes; one factor dimension dim H is the centralizer cost for that cycle.

Non-density for semisimple integral fibres. Let 𝓧/Z[S⁻¹] have smooth geometrically connected generic fibre X of positive dimension. For an integral polarized pure compatible system with integral Frobenius and rational Frobenius characteristic polynomials outside S, uniform coefficient filtration and strongly c-balanced monodromy, assume A≥(dim X+dim H)/c. The integral points whose global coefficient-group representations are G-completely reducible are not Zariski dense in X. Fix the coefficient permutation representation and enlarge S only by finitely many primes.

stages.title: Balanced associated gradeds and codimension
stages.description:
Define central weights, induced Levi filtrations, balance and bifiltered Frobenius types. Derive balance from global purity over Q, finite graded types, the corrected stable-Levi argument, root-count bounds and the fixed-type codimension theorem.

Central weights of filtrations. For a characteristic-zero reductive group S, let a_S=X_*(Z(S)°)⊗Q, equivalently the Q-dual of rational characters of S via the nondegenerate central pairing. The weight w_S(μ) of a rational cocharacter μ is its projection to a_S. For a Levi M⊂G, restriction of rational characters gives a canonical inclusion ι_GM:a_G→a_M and a splitting of the opposite projection. Define the modular character γ_P as the inverse determinant of Ad on Lie(P), with additive pairing against cocharacters.

Filtrations induced on a Levi quotient. Let G be as in M2.2, P a Richardson parabolic with Levi quotient M and F a G-filtration. Choose a splitting cocharacter of F taking values in P; its projection defines a filtration F_M independent of this choice. On a flag variety the fixed points of a cocharacter in a given homogeneous orbit are conjugate under its centralizer; use this to establish independence. For GL(V), F_M is the filtration induced by F on the graded vector space of the P-flag.

Balanced, weakly balanced and semibalanced filtrations. For F and P→M as above, F is balanced when w_M(F_M)=ι_GM(w_G(F)); weakly balanced when ⟨γ_P,F_M⟩=0; and semibalanced when ⟨γ_P,F_M⟩≤0. Balance implies weak balance, which implies semibalance. The latter two test one modular character and are generally weaker than the vector identity defining balance. The restriction to G° preserves all three conditions.

Global purity forces balance over Q. Let ρ:G_Q→G(Q_p) be crystalline at p, pure of integral Weil weight w on the chosen faithful representation, with image contained in P. The de Rham Hodge filtration induced on the corresponding inner Levi quotient is balanced relative to P. In the GL case this says every global graded subquotient has Hodge–Tate average w/2, using the convention that a Tate object of geometric Frobenius q has de Rham weight 1. This global assertion is over Q; it is false in this form for arbitrary number fields with different embeddings.

Bifiltered Frobenius objects and graded types. A bifiltered coefficient Frobenius object is (V,φ,F,f), with Hodge G-filtration F, φ-stable auxiliary G-filtration f and the given semilinear coefficient structure. Its graded type is the G-conjugacy class of (P_f,φ_M,F_M). Forget the numerical indexing of f when defining this type, while retaining the full Hodge indexing of F_M. This forgotten auxiliary indexing is necessary for finiteness; types are not unfiltered characteristic polynomials.

Finite cyclic cocycles in unipotent groups. Let U be a characteristic-zero unipotent algebraic group and ψ an automorphism of finite order dividing r≥1. If uψ(u)⋯ψ^(r−1)(u)=1, there is v∈U with u=v⁻¹ψ(v). Thus H¹(C_r,U)=1 for this action. The finite-order condition on ψ is essential to this argument.

Levi factors stable under semisimple Frobenius. If a semisimple element φ of the ambient characteristic-zero group normalizes the connected parabolic P, a unipotent conjugate of a chosen Levi of P is φ-stable. In the norm argument choose r killing the induced finite component action. The relevant cocycle u lies in Z_U(φ^r), where conjugation by φ has order dividing r; do not assume conjugation has finite order on all of U.

Finitely many local types from global semisimplification. For fixed global coefficient-group semisimplification ρ^ss and fixed residue Frobenius data, the local bifiltered objects obtained by choosing a global semisimplification flag have only finitely many graded types, and their induced Hodge filtrations are balanced. The assertion concerns the quotient type forgetting auxiliary flag indices. It does not say there are finitely many flags or extensions.

Root pairing for opposite flag directions. Fix positive roots Σ⁺ and standard parabolics P,Q containing the positive Borel; let Σ_P,Σ_Q be their full Lie root sets, and Δ_P,Δ_Q the simple roots of their Levis. For w with w⁻¹Δ_P⊂Σ⁺ and wΔ_Q⊂Σ⁺, the map β↦−wβ bijects {β∈Σ\Σ_Q : wβ>0} with {α∈Σ\Σ_P : w⁻¹α>0}; its inverse is α↦−w⁻¹α. Each set has size length(w). The two sign equivalences are β∈Σ\Σ_Q ⇒ (wβ>0 iff −wβ∉Σ_P) and the analogous statement with P,Q,w⁻¹.

Semibalanced fixed-graded fibre bound. Let G=H^c over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, with H connected reductive of rank t, and let F₀ have uniform single-factor adjoint profile h. Put A=Σ_(a>0)h^a and B=Σ_(a>0)a h^a. For an integer e>0, assume A≥e/c and B>T(e/c)+T((h⁰−t)/2+e/c), with both T arguments in its domain. For every parabolic P and every prescribed induced Levi filtration, its semibalanced fibre inside the orbit G·F₀ has codimension at least e. In the single connected group case, the stronger LV hypotheses A≥e and B>T(e)+T(h⁰/2+e) give codimension strictly greater than e for balanced fibres.

Dimension of Frobenius-stable graded pairs. Fix a semisimple Frobenius φ in the algebraic coefficient normalizer. Pairs (P,F_M) with φ∈P and prescribed conjugacy class of the quotient filtered Frobenius data form finitely many centralizer orbits, hence have dimension at most dim Z_G(φ). For an arbitrary φ replace it by φ^ss and use φ-stable Levi reduction; the resulting dimension bound uses dim Z_G(φ^ss). Apply cyclewise to bound the cost by dim H.

Fixed-type codimension under balanced monodromy. Let the coefficient system have uniform single-factor profile h, rank t for H, strongly c-balanced monodromy and a balanced reference graded type. Given a positive integer e, assume A≥(e+dim H)/c and B>T((e+dim H)/c)+T((h⁰−t)/2+(e+dim H)/c), with valid T arguments. In the monodromy period orbit, the locus admitting a φ-stable auxiliary filtration with that graded type has codimension at least e.

stages.title: The coefficient non-density theorem
stages.description:
Combine global-type finiteness, balanced local types, strongly balanced monodromy and p-adic transcendence. Deduce non-density of all integral points under the two single-factor adjoint Hodge inequalities.

The coefficient non-density theorem. Let 𝓧/Z[S⁻¹] have smooth geometrically connected generic fibre X of dimension d>0. Let V be a pure polarized integral Hodge–Deligne system with integral Frobenius and rational Frobenius characteristic polynomials outside S, an equidimensional E-module of classical rank N and the required coefficient pairing. Assume a uniform factor profile h, strongly c-balanced differential monodromy relative to residue Frobenius and, writing t=rank H, A≥(d+dim H)/c and B>T((d+dim H)/c)+T((h⁰−t)/2+(d+dim H)/c). All T arguments must be in [0,dim H]. Then 𝓧(Z[S⁻¹]) is not Zariski dense in X. No semisimplicity hypothesis is imposed on the actual fibres.

stages.title: Higher-dimensional Lawrence–Venkatesh non-density
stages.description:
Compare crystalline fibre functors, place the Hodge torus in the Galois image, choose a uniformly bounded small-centralizer prime and apply the classical bad-filtration estimate. Prove the published Theorem 10.1 and its stronger conditional finiteness clause, and state the corrected independent point-count bound.

Comparing crystalline and forgetful fibre functors. For the neutral tensor category generated by a crystalline p-adic representation V with its intersection/similitude tensors, the forgetful fibre functor and underlying D_cris fibre functor become tensor-isomorphic over Q̄_p. Such an isomorphism identifies their Tannaka groups by conjugacy and preserves every defining pairing tensor. This is an existence statement over the algebraic closure, not a canonical rational comparison.

The Hodge torus in the Galois image. For primitive middle cohomology of a smooth projective variety over Q_p with good reduction, transport the Hodge cocharacter through the crystalline/forgetful tensor comparison. The Zariski closure of the local p-adic Galois image contains a torus conjugate over Q̄_p to the Hodge torus. Apply the tensor-compatible Sen/Wintenberger splitting supplied by R06.2; its compatibility with defining form tensors upgrades the GL assertion to the full similitude group.

A bounded prime with small Frobenius centralizer. For a fixed smooth projective family over Z[S⁻¹], with fixed primitive middle-cohomology Hodge type and group GAut of the intersection pairing, there is L such that every integral fibre admits a prime ℓ≤L outside S with dim Z_GAut((φ_crys,ℓ)^ss)≤h⁰. Choose an auxiliary prime p outside S large enough for the common shifted Fontaine–Laffaille interval. The bound is uniform in the integral point, not an effective formula for L.

Bad self-dual filtrations have large codimension. For a classical similitude space V, Frobenius φ and prescribed filtered Frobenius graded objects of a φ-stable self-dual auxiliary flag, put z=dim Z_GAut(φ^ss). Require each nonzero graded object to have Hodge-weight average r/2, and set e>0. If A≥z+e and B>T(z+e)+T(h⁰/2+z+e), with valid T arguments, the self-dual Hodge filtrations admitting such a flag have codimension at least e in their fixed Hodge-type flag variety. Self-dual middle pieces retain their pairing tensor.

Classical semisimplification fibres are nondense. Under the two numerical inequalities of the following theorem, fix ℓ∉S and a residue point with crystalline semisimple centralizer dimension at most h⁰. Integral points in its residue disk whose global ℓ-adic representations have a prescribed semisimplification form a nondense subset of the base. Global semisimplification flags are self-dual after pairing dual constituents, and each graded Hodge average is r/2 by global purity over Q.

Higher-dimensional integral-point non-density. Let π:𝓩→𝓨 be smooth projective with geometrically connected relative dimension r, a relative ample class, and smooth geometrically connected generic base Y/Q of dimension d>0. Let V be primitive degree-r cohomology and assume geometric monodromy contains GAut(V,⟨,⟩)°. For its adjoint profile require A≥h⁰+d and B>T(h⁰+d)+T(3h⁰/2+d), with valid T arguments. Then 𝓨(Z[S⁻¹]) is not Zariski dense in Y. The theorem is the classical first instance of the shared period/codimension mechanism; the bounded-prime step is distinct from the coefficient-orbit construction.

Finiteness under monodromy on every subvariety. In the preceding setup, assume every positive-dimensional geometrically irreducible subvariety of Y retains full connected primitive monodromy after passage to its smooth locus and finite field of definition, with the required rational arithmetic model or restriction-of-scalars comparison. Then the integral point set is finite. This stronger monodromy condition is an additional hypothesis; it is not established for the universal hypersurface family by large generic monodromy alone.

A point-count bound for Frobenius centralizers. For a smooth degree-d hypersurface of dimension n≥2 over F_q, let b>0 be the dimension of primitive middle cohomology. For every integer N≥1 satisfying q^((n/2+1)·2N)<b/3, the GL-centralizer of semisimple Frobenius has dimension at most 3b²/N. Thus the largest such positive N gives the strongest stated estimate whenever one exists. The assertion is independent of the bounded-prime argument and is not used to claim a computable universal prime bound.

stages.title: Eulerian profiles and numerical criteria
stages.description:
Compute classical adjoint profiles of twisted abelian hypersurfaces and show that enough independent factors satisfy the coefficient inequalities. Derive projective hypersurface Hodge numbers from residues, their Eulerian asymptotics and the large-dimension/large-degree LV inequalities.

Classical adjoint profiles from Eulerian multiplicities. For smooth ample hypersurfaces in an n-dimensional abelian variety, n≥2 and normalized degree d>0, import m_q=d·A(n,q), 0≤q<n, and N=n!d from SC.3. The adjoint weights of GL_N, GSp_N or GO_N are obtained from End(V), Sym²(V) or ∧²(V), with the scalar multiplier direction in degree zero for the similitude groups. For the geometric parity choices GL in either parity, GSp when n is even and GO when n is odd, 2h⁰<dim H+rank H. In particular (h⁰−rank H)/2<A. The opposite, nongeometric parity choices are not part of this assertion.

Difference distribution of Eulerian weights. For n≥2 define α_q=A(n,q)/n!, extended by zero outside 0≤q<n, and β_j=Σ_q α_q α_(q−j), j∈Z. This is the distribution of the difference of two independent ascent counts, not of their sum without recentering. It is a symmetric, finitely supported probability distribution and is the normalized GL adjoint multiplicity profile.

Second moment and log-concavity. For n≥2, the Eulerian difference law has mean zero, second moment (n+1)/6 and log-concave masses. Its one-copy centered ascent law has variance (n+1)/12. Log-concavity here is on contiguous integer support, so convolution and reflection preserve it; zeros outside the support are handled explicitly.

The central Eulerian convolution mass is at most one half. For every n≥2 the difference law satisfies β₀≤1/2. For n≥9, assuming β₀>1/2 and using symmetry and log-concavity forces cumulative tails Σ_(j≥k)β_j<Σ_(j≥k)1/(2·3^j), k≥1, which gives a strict upper bound of 3/2 for its second moment, contradicting (n+1)/6≥5/3. Verify 2≤n≤8 by exact Eulerian integer sums.

Enough independent factors satisfy the coefficient inequalities. For the geometric Eulerian profile above and every fixed integer e>0, there is an integer c₀≥1 such that all c≥c₀ satisfy A≥(e+dim H)/c and B>T((e+dim H)/c)+T((h⁰−rank H)/2+(e+dim H)/c), with arguments in the domain. The same choice implies the simpler semisimple numerical inequality. No bound uniform in arbitrary Hodge profiles is asserted.

Primitive hypersurface Hodge numbers from the Jacobian ring. For a smooth degree-d hypersurface in P^n over C, primitive middle Hodge multiplicity h^{p,n−1−p} is the coefficient of t^((p+1)d−n−1) in (1+t+⋯+t^(d−2))^(n+1), for 0≤p<n. Use the residue/Jacobian identification and the regular-sequence Hilbert series for the n+1 partial derivatives. This supplies the omitted justification of LV (10.6).

Eulerian asymptotics of projective hypersurface cohomology. Fix n≥2. As d→∞, primitive h^{p,n−1−p}(d)∼d^n A(n,p)/n! for 0≤p<n. After adjoint formation, h^a/(d^(2n)/2)→β_a for the orthogonal or symplectic similitude group. The universal parameter space has dimension binomial(n+d,d)−1=O(d^n), hence dim Y/h⁰→0. Here n is ambient dimension; the hypersurface dimension is n−1.

Normal-limit estimates for adjoint Eulerian weights. As n→∞ the centered ascent count divided by √n converges in law to N(0,1/12); its independent difference converges to N(0,1/6). Consequently Σ_(a>0)aβ_a≥C√n for some C>0 and all sufficiently large n. Log-concavity and the variance imply β₀<40/√n for sufficiently large n. For each fixed c>0 the sum of the largest c/√n fraction of difference weights is o(√n).

Large ambient dimension and degree satisfy the LV inequalities. There is n₀ such that for every n≥n₀ there exists D₀(n) with the published LV inequalities A≥h⁰+dim Y and B>T(h⁰+dim Y)+T(3h⁰/2+dim Y) for all d≥D₀(n), for the primitive universal degree-d hypersurface profile in P^n. All top-sum arguments lie in their finite domains. Limits are taken first in d for fixed n, then in n; no joint-limit uniformity is claimed.

stages.title: Projective hypersurface application
stages.description:
Construct the universal smooth degree-d family with its actual coefficient-space dimension, apply the parity-correct Beauville monodromy input in a safe range, and prove non-density of integral parameters for large ambient dimension and degree.

Universal smooth projective hypersurfaces. For n≥2,d≥2 let Y_nd be the smooth-hypersurface open of P(H⁰(P^n,O(d))) over Z after specifying its discriminant and any required inverted primes. It has dimension binomial(n+d,d)−1 and carries the universal smooth projective degree-d hypersurface with relative O(1). Primitive middle cohomology is the kernel of the Lefschetz pairing map, with its nondegenerate intersection form. This parameter space retains equations up to scalar; it is not the quotient by PGL_(n+1).

Large connected monodromy for universal hypersurfaces. For universal smooth degree-d hypersurfaces in P^n over C, in the safe range n≥4,d≥4, the Zariski closure of primitive middle-cohomology monodromy contains the identity component of the intersection-form group: symplectic for middle dimension n−1 odd, special orthogonal for n−1 even. Use Beauville’s arithmetic monodromy theorems, with their low-degree finite exceptions excluded by this range. The scalar similitude direction is arithmetic and need not occur in geometric monodromy.

Non-density of integral hypersurface parameters. There exists n₀≥4 and for each n≥n₀ a bound D₀(n)≥4 such that for all d≥D₀(n), Y_nd(Z[S⁻¹]) is contained in a proper algebraic subset of Y_nd,Q, for every finite set S after the required model primes are included. This is the fixed-integral-model interpretation of projective hypersurfaces with good reduction. It proves non-density in the universal parameter space and makes no finiteness claim for its PGL quotient.

stages.title: Hypersurface Shafarevich finiteness
stages.description:
Parameterize smooth ample divisors of fixed class, transfer integral points by finite étale restriction of scalars and resolve their dense closure over a smooth open. Apply the coefficient theorem to nontranslation families, obtain primitive finiteness, pass through finite stabilizer quotients and rational translation descent, and treat the abelian-surface case by fixed-genus curve finiteness and a positive Hom lattice.

Good reduction and primitive hypersurfaces. Fix a number field K, finite S, an abelian variety A/K with abelian scheme model 𝓐 over O_K[S⁻¹], and a smooth ample effective divisor H⊂A. Good reduction outside S means its schematic closure in 𝓐 is smooth over O_K[S⁻¹]. The translation stabilizer Stab(H) is the finite group scheme of a with H+a=H; H is primitive when Stab(H)(K̄)={0}. Only nonzero translations are excluded, since translation by zero always fixes H.

A parameter space for smooth ample divisors. For A/K and fixed ample numerical class φ, construct a finite-type quasi-projective K-scheme parameterizing smooth effective divisors with class φ, together with its universal divisor in A×Y. Use a Hilbert polynomial for a fixed auxiliary ample line bundle, and the union of the corresponding numerical-class components. Over an enlarged S, closures with good reduction give integral points of this parameter space. Translation by A acts algebraically and preserves the numerical class.

Restriction of scalars and integral parameters. After enlarging a finite set S′ of rational primes so O_K[S⁻¹] is finite étale over Z[S′⁻¹], the quasi-projective divisor parameter scheme admits a scheme-valued Weil restriction X/Q with an integral model. Its integral points identify with the original O_K[S⁻¹]-points. Use the existing A6 restriction-of-scalars functor and its universal property; use A6’s imported quasi-projective representability criterion. The abelian variety restriction is again abelian in this finite étale setting.

Reducing a dense arithmetic closure to a smooth base. Let a set of integral points in a finite-type characteristic-zero parameter scheme be Zariski dense in an irreducible component C of its closure. Resolve C properly by X→C, isomorphic over a dense smooth open U. The points in U have unique rational lifts, and after spreading out the proper map these lifts are integral by the valuative criterion. They are dense in X. Points outside U are handled through the finitely many closure components or Noetherian induction, rather than by assuming every rational point of C lifts.

Nonconstant abelian-divisor families are arithmetically nondense. For a smooth positive-dimensional arithmetic base X/Q arising above, suppose its universal family of primitive smooth ample divisors in A is nonconstant up to geometric translation. Assume n=dim A≥4, or n=3 and normalized degree d=φ^n/n! avoids SC.5’s exceptional degrees D_j, j≥1. Then its integral parameter set is not Zariski dense. Choose c using the Eulerian numerical criterion and then use SC.8’s conjugate-uniform torsion orbit to construct the compatible coefficient system.

Primitive hypersurface Shafarevich finiteness. For A/K, good reduction outside S and fixed ample class φ, primitive smooth hypersurfaces in class φ with good reduction outside S form finitely many geometric translation classes when n≥4, or when n=3 and d=φ³/6 is not an exceptional D_j, j≥1. Translation orbits in the divisor parameter scheme are closed because A is proper. Hence an irreducible component containing a dense arithmetic set either lies in one orbit or contradicts the nontranslation-family theorem.

Finite stabilizers and primitive isogeny quotients. Every smooth ample hypersurface H in A is the inverse image of a primitive smooth ample divisor H′ in A/T, where T=Stab(H) is finite and the quotient isogeny has degree |T|. Its normalized degree satisfies d(H)=|T|d(H′). For fixed numerical class, only finitely many possible kernels T occur: their orders divide d(H), and each lies in the finite torsion subgroup A[m] for a common multiple m. Descent of the quotient and H′ is over K.

From geometric translations to A(K)-translations. For a fixed K-defined smooth ample divisor H with finite stabilizer T, K-defined geometric translates are parameterized by (A/T)(K) inside its orbit. Their A(K)-translation classes inject into (A/T)(K)/πA(K), a finite group by weak Mordell–Weil for the isogeny π. For primitive H, T=0 and geometric translation between two K-defined divisors is uniquely K-rational. Thus a finite list of geometric translation classes gives a finite list modulo A(K).

Shafarevich finiteness for all smooth ample hypersurfaces. For A/K of dimension n≥4 and fixed ample numerical class φ, smooth hypersurfaces representing φ with good reduction outside S form finitely many A(K)-translation classes. For n=3 the same holds if d=φ³/6 is not divisible by any exceptional D_j, j≥1. Equivalently φ³ is not divisible by the source integer d_i=6D_(i−1) for i≥2. The primitive theorem only excludes equality d=D_j; the all-hypersurface theorem must exclude divisibility.

The abelian-surface case through curves. For an abelian surface A/K, fixed ample class φ and finite S, smooth hypersurfaces with good reduction outside S form finitely many A(K)-translation classes. Adjunction fixes their genus g=1+φ²/2≥2. Shafarevich finiteness for curves gives finitely many curve isomorphism classes. For each curve, pointed maps to A are homomorphisms from its Jacobian, and the fixed divisor class bounds a positive definite Rosati quadratic form on the finitely generated Hom group.
